<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="שבט_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518917129_theRebbe_291" batchId="meluket-_D7_A9_D7_91_D7_98_meluket__BH_POST_1766518917129_theRebbe_291__p002">
  <section v="3">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the phrase "Ki Tisa" could be interpreted as lifting the head from its fall, but notes that after Yom Kippur the sin's residue only affects the concealment of the superrational will within the inner faculties.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And to note,</t>
    <t s="1">in Likkutei Torah, the discourse "Shuvah Yisrael... Ki Khasalta BaAvonecha,"</t>
    <t s="2">it is explained as a parable of a person whose foot stumbles, causing his head to fall downward.</t>
    <t s="3">Based on this, one could say that the meaning of "Ki Tisa et Rosh Bnei Yisrael" is to lift the head from its fall downward.</t>
    <t s="4">And one can give a reason why in the above discourses it is not explained this way,</t>
    <t s="5">because this portion was said after Yom Kippur,</t>
    <t s="6">after the Holy One, blessed be He, was appeased to Yisrael with joy and a full heart, and said to Moshe, "I have forgiven as you have said."</t>
    <t s="7">And the impression of the sin that remains after Yom Kippur is</t>
    <t s="8">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="9">only regarding the fact that the will that is above intellect did not shine in revelation within the inner faculties,</t>
    <t s="10">therefore it says "Ki Tisa et Rosh Bnei Yisrael."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="4">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section discusses the concept of the "horn" (keren) of Yisrael, which is above the head and represents the level of Kesser, and distinguishes between the encompassing light of the skull and the horn as an encompassing that transcends connection to the inner.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And it is written,</t>
    <t s="2">"He has cut down in fierce anger all the horn of Yisrael,"</t>
    <t s="3">that through sins there is a descent even in the aspect of the horn that is above the head.</t>
    <t s="4">Therefore Moshe said, "With what shall the horn of Yisrael be exalted?"</t>
    <t s="5">that it is necessary to elevate and exalt the horn that is above the head.</t>
    <t s="6">And it is explained in Likkutei Torah,</t>
    <t s="7">that "horn" is the aspect of Kesser.</t>
    <t s="8">And explanation is needed,</t>
    <t s="9">for the fact that the horn is above the head is</t>
    <t s="10">(not only above the brain within the head, but)</t>
    <t s="11">also above the skull,</t>
    <t s="12">and according to what is known that "Gulgulta"</t>
    <t s="13">(the skull that covers the brain)</t>
    <t s="14">is the aspect of Kesser,</t>
    <t s="15">what is the superiority of the horn over the head?</t>
    <t s="16">And one can say,</t>
    <t s="17">that "Gulgulta" is an encompassing that is related to the inner,</t>
    <t s="18">analogous to the skull in a person that encompasses the brain but is related to it,</t>
    <t s="19">and "horn" is an encompassing that is above any relation to the inner.</t>
    <t s="20">And as explained in many places</t>
    <t s="21">in the interpretation of the verse,</t>
    <t s="22">"And He will exalt the horn of His people,"</t>
    <t s="23">that it refers to the Atzmus of Ein Sof, which is above the encompassing.</t>
    <t s="24">And likewise it is in the soul,</t>
    <t s="25">that the horn of the soul is the essence of the soul.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="5">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the descent of the soul's essence due to sin is not from the influence of revealed faculties, but because the purpose of its descent into the body was not fulfilled, analogous to a horn cut off from the head.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And it is necessary to understand what Moshe said, "With what shall the horn of Yisrael be exalted?"</t>
    <t s="1">For at first glance,</t>
    <t s="2">how can there be a descent in the essence of the soul?</t>
    <t s="3">And one can give the explanation of this,</t>
    <t s="4">that the intention of the soul's descent below is in order to act upon the body,</t>
    <t s="5">therefore,</t>
    <t s="6">when it does not fulfill the intention, a descent occurs in all its levels,</t>
    <t s="7">even in its essence</t>
    <t s="8">(that descended below).</t>
    <t s="9">And based on this,</t>
    <t s="10">the descent caused by sin in the level of the head of the soul,</t>
    <t s="11">is because relative to this level there is significance to the revealed faculties</t>
    <t s="12">(since it is an encompassing that is related to the inner),</t>
    <t s="13">and therefore matters of the revealed faculties cause a change in it</t>
    <t s="14">(except that the change is only regarding its revelation,</t>
    <t s="15">as above in section 2),</t>
    <t s="16">and the descent caused by sin in the essence of the soul is not that matters of the revealed faculties cause a change in it,</t>
    <t s="17">but rather because the intention for which it descended below was not fulfilled.</t>
    <t s="18">And one can say,</t>
    <t s="19">that this is what is written, "He has cut down... the horn of Yisrael,"</t>
    <t s="20">for just as with a horn in its simple sense,</t>
    <t s="21">the change that occurs in the horn by being cut off from the head</t>
    <t s="22">(that it does not have the strength it had initially)</t>
    <t s="23">is not that the head causes a change in the horn, but rather because it was cut off from the head,</t>
    <t s="24">so too is it regarding the horn of the soul,</t>
    <t s="25">that the change that occurs in it through sin is from the aspect that it does not act upon the revealed faculties</t>
    <t s="26">(and does not fulfill the intention of its descent below).</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
